global_gaps: The original fiscal-substitutes matching question directly overlaps the published Kojima–Sun–Yu (2024) article, and the revised manuscript does not cite or distinguish it.
The narrow capped two-worker rebate result has no targeted priority check against budget-constrained substitutes policy and no welfare or financing model.
uncertainty: The mathematical statements are coherent within the stated finite EX model, conditional on the verified published Murota theorems. Publication novelty of the narrow budget result has not been established; no formal proof assistant check was performed.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: EX move/swap cancellation must respect the changed coordinate and all demand ties.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: No mismatch within finite real-price domain.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Demand ties could break a unique-choice shortcut, but the maximal-overlap selection covers them.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Both sides of each exchange need the same modular incidence.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The iff is for EX; GS preservation is claimed only on the EX domain.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Nonmodular schedules may also preserve EX for a specific valuation; the paper acknowledges this.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: All-real-price necessity needs a strict witness when the two-worker inequality fails.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The necessity need not hold on a nonnegative-only price domain; the manuscript says so.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Tied demand at equality does not invalidate weak EX or GS.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: g=q-v is an algebraic implementation and requires full valuation knowledge.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: No bounded expenditure, information feasibility, or welfare claim follows.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Other feasible policy classes may fail to implement the target; this is explicitly unrestricted.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Weakly increasing effective own-wage costs must be the sole changed price coordinate.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: Only demand GS on nonnegative actual wages is proved; common-wage equilibrium is excluded.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Employer-specific wedges can obstruct equilibrium despite each firm's GS demand.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Allocated positive-max-value workers must yield zero marginal firm profit at chosen wages.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The maximized objective is adjusted private value, not fiscally net social welfare.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Government payments can alter allocation rankings relative to production value.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Murota 6.1(9) closure and 9.4 intersection must allow real values; dummy-price conversion and LP duality must follow.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The LP claim is existence of an integral optimum, not integrality of every vertex or novelty of the theorem.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Ordinary GS alone may need additional hypotheses; the proof assumes the stronger EX property.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Four bundle profits at both prices must show unique choices.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The example demonstrates GS failure, not equilibrium nonexistence.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Market equilibrium might still exist for some multi-firm profile.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: The coverage function must be submodular yet fail the full three-worker exchange and GS tests.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The counterexample says nothing about all submodular valuations.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Diminishing marginal returns alone misses cross-bundle exchange structure.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: The headcount-increment necessity witness must eliminate swaps.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: The equivalence is for additive value plus cardinality term, not arbitrary baseline valuations.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Nonadditive values can change the exact headcount condition.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: The firm objective includes fiscal payments by definition.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: No financing or social welfare primitive appears in the model.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: Adjusted private value can disagree with production or fiscally net welfare.

claim_reviews.weakest_link: Worst-case spending is exactly 2r when at least two firms exist; robust EX requires 2r>=kappa.
claim_reviews.scope_or_number_mismatch: B>=kappa is only for a uniform nonnegative singleton rebate with a cap on every feasible allocation.
claim_reviews.competing_explanation: A particular realized valuation may need no rebate; an alternative policy could cost less.
